newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Sphinx unit sales to aid flagging solvency.
newsitem.headline: Sphinx unit sales to aid flagging solvency.

text.p: Sanitary ware maker Sphinx Gustavsberg saw solvency ratios decline further in the 1996/97 financial year, but said sales of non-core businesses would improve them slightly.
Group capital as a percentage of total assets dwindled to a meagre 18.1 percent in the 1996/97 financial year ended March 31 from a year-earlier 26.5 percent.
However Sphinx said the recently announced sale of its Schock Bad bathroom appliances and Sphinx Tiles activities would improve balance sheet ratios.

"After completion of the transactions, solvency will increase to 21.1 percent and the guaranteed capital (shareholders' equity plus subordinated loans) will amount to 34.3 percent of the balance sheet total," the company said.
Sphinx Gustavsberg earlier reported a net loss for the 1996/97 year of 45.1 million guilders, up from a 33.1 million guilder loss in the previous year.
